title: The H1 must be followed by a summary blockquote

spec.name: llms.txt (llmstxt.org)
spec.normative_quote: A blockquote with a short summary of the project, containing key information necessary for understanding the rest of the file
spec.note: conformance_testable is false, per the divergence recorded in policy_note: the spec's own prose marks only the H1 as strictly required. Verified against a live fetch of https://llmstxt.org/ on 2026-07-30. Corrects a prior defect: 'as would be immediately useful to an LLM' was fabricated and does not appear on the page; the real item 3 also reads 'the project', not 'the project or site'.

policy_note: Migrated verbatim from validate-llms-txt.mjs:69-72 (pre-pilot): 'required by this validator; the spec's own prose marks only the H1 as strictly required, but every real-world llms.txt -- including this site's -- includes it, and the team's validator contract treats it as required.' This is a declared, reviewable local convention, not a claim about llmstxt.org conformance.
applicability: An llms.txt body whose first non-blank line is a valid H1.
expectation: The next non-blank line after the H1 matches /^>\s+\S/.

cases.name: H1 present, nothing at all follows (bqLine is null, not merely non-matching)

known-answer fixture: an unlinked URL, a dangling section, and no blockquote all flag together (REVERSAL 2 -- a shared multi-violation input is a legal failed case; its expect lists every id the input emits). The fixture moved to v2 violations in the same commit as the v2 relaxation: under v1 it used a bare bullet with no URL and a prose-only section, both legal now, which would have quietly reduced this case to a single-violation input.
